solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fiddler taking six out on walk to see gymnast

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece placed on another follows it

parts.note: to tramp is to walk heavily or a long way

indicators.note: taking ... out, around the number, says those letters are removed from the fiddler
taking ... out, around the number, says those letters are removed from the fiddler

parts.note: a fiddler is a violinist
VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone heads out for a stroll with a group of fiddlers to watch a gymnastics display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking ... out' straddles 'six', removing it as a Roman numeral; 'on' places the result after the walk in this across clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A trampolinist performs gymnastic routines on a trampoline, so is a kind of gymnast.

clue.text: Upset German with a Christian dish

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: mit is the German word for with
Christian Bale is the Hollywood actor, so 'a Christian' is a Bale

explanation.surface: A German, upset, sits with a Christian over a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'German' is not a person but labels the language: 'German with' is MIT, which 'Upset' turns into TIM. 'a Christian' is a man with that first name, the actor Christian Bale.
explanation.definitionFit: A timbale is a baked dish of minced meat or fish cooked in a drum-shaped mould.

clue.text: He leaves ornate covering in residential location

indicators.note: leaves means departs, so those letters go out of the word

parts.note: a headdress is an ornamental covering for the head
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man walks away from a decorated covering on a house.
explanation.definitionFit: An address is the details of where someone lives, a residential location.

clue.text: Cake not eaten loosely covered by priest

indicators.note: in a down clue a piece covered by another sits below it
loosely means without fixed order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cake left uneaten is lightly covered over by a priest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loosely' rearranges NOTEATEN to ANETTONE, placed under P.
explanation.definitionFit: Panettone is a tall Italian sweet bread-cake with dried fruit, eaten at Christmas.

clue.text: Ex-President wearing 50s brand

indicators.note: the fifties wear the president like a garment, so he goes inside them

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral 50, so two of them are 50s
Abe Lincoln is a former US president

explanation.surface: A former president dressed in fifties-style fashion from some label.
explanation.walkthrough: '50s' is not a decade but two fifties, L and L.
explanation.definitionFit: A label is a brand name under which goods, especially clothes or records, are sold.

clue.text: Party without six-packs? It's not possible

definitions.note: a colloquial way of saying something cannot be done

parts.note: a do without six-packs has no cans of beer: NO CAN
a do is a party or social event

explanation.surface: A party with no beer laid on is simply out of the question.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue's order is reversed in the answer: the description of the party's lack comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: The colloquial phrase is a blunt refusal meaning a request cannot be granted.

clue.text: Sauna oddly housing large brown dried thing

indicators.note: housing means holding inside, so the other letters go within
oddly picks the first, third and fifth letters of the word

parts.note: tan is a light brown colour

explanation.surface: Someone in a sauna gets a big brown tan and dries out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sauna oddly' supplies the outer shell that is 'housing' the other letters; 'dried thing' is a deliberately vague definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A sultana is a seedless grape that has been dried, a vague but fair description.

clue.text: Steaming fresh larks around centre of griddle

indicators.note: fresh means newly made, so these letters are formed into a new arrangement
centre of picks the middle letter of the seven-letter word

explanation.surface: Fresh birds are cooked around the middle of a hot griddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' looks like a container signal but is part of the fodder for 'fresh'. 'Steaming' suggests cooking but is British slang for very drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Steaming is British slang for heavily intoxicated, and the phrase is a simile for extreme drunkenness.

clue.text: Fast male animal brought back nothing

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep

indicators.note: brought back means returned, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: nada is slang, from Spanish, for nothing

explanation.surface: A quick male beast returned with nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramadan is the Muslim month of fasting from dawn to dusk, so a fast.

clue.text: Abbreviated writing on reverse subtly illuminated

indicators.note: LIT written on BACK follows it in an across clue

parts.note: the reverse of something is its back
lit is a short form of literature, writing

explanation.surface: Shorthand notes on the back of a page are faintly lit up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reverse' looks like a turnaround signal but is simply the back of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Backlit means lit from behind, giving a soft, indirect light.

clue.text: Overly tetchy hotel boss initially hurries cleaners

parts.note: too means excessively, overly

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of each of the three words

parts.note: rushes means hurries

explanation.surface: An irritable hotel manager rushes around the cleaning staff.
explanation.definitionFit: Toothbrushes are the brushes used to clean teeth.

clue.text: Attention being held by lair closest by

indicators.note: being held by means being contained within the other word

parts.note: a nest is an animal's den or lair
to have someone's ear is to have their attention

explanation.surface: A beast's den nearby catches someone's notice.
explanation.definitionFit: Nearest is the superlative of near, the same as closest in distance.

clue.text: Pine flagons stripped twice in the distant past

parts.note: to long for something is to pine for it

indicators.note: stripping a word removes its outer letters, and doing it twice takes two from each end

explanation.surface: Old flagons made of pine, twice scraped clean, from olden times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stripped twice' peels FLAGONS to LAGON, then to AGO.
explanation.definitionFit: Long ago means at a time far back, the distant past.

clue.text: Declares part of song that's ultimately been lifted

indicators.note: the ultimate, final letter is lifted away from the phrase

parts.note: a verse is one section of a song, so a part of a song is a verse

explanation.surface: Someone claims a section of a song has been plagiarised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifted' suggests copying, but it removes the last letter of A VERSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To aver is to state firmly, so avers means declares.

clue.text: Manipulative healthcare worker

parts.note: manipulative suggests a scheming person, but here it means one who treats by manipulating bones and joints

explanation.surface: A scheming nurse or doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: An osteopath treats patients by manipulating the skeleton and muscles.

clue.text: Chuckles when wife abandons Birdsong

indicators.note: abandons means leaves, so that letter is removed

parts.note: twittering is the chirping song of birds

explanation.surface: A man laughs when his wife walks out on him for a bird-call outing.
explanation.definitionFit: Tittering is nervous or suppressed laughter, so chuckles in the verb sense.

clue.text: Sailor with small shelter keeping home dry

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

indicators.note: keeping means holding, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a tent is a simple shelter
in means at home

explanation.surface: A seaman with a little tent keeps his home dry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dry' at the end looks like part of the camping scene but means teetotal.
explanation.definitionFit: Dry in the sense of not drinking alcohol is what abstinent means.

clue.text: Expert more animated after drink

indicators.note: in a down clue the second piece comes after, below, the first

parts.note: to sup is to drink

indicators.note: animated means lively and moved about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A specialist becomes livelier after a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A supremo is a person in overall charge, here treated as a top master of a field.

clue.text: Sea hazard from bleak Cape circles northwards

indicators.note: northwards says the hidden letters are read backwards
from says the answer is taken out of the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Ships rounding a bleak cape face danger as they head north.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'northwards' means read upwards; 'circles' is part of the hidden text, not an indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Pack ice, floating sea ice crowded together, is a danger to shipping.

clue.text: Nasty biter somewhat chafing at orthodontist

indicators.note: somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A patient with bad teeth gets irritated at a dentist who straightens teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: A gator, short for alligator, is a reptile with a fearsome bite.

clue.text: African money pinched by doctor and a relative

indicators.note: pinched by means squeezed between, so the money goes inside

parts.note: GP, general practitioner, is a family doctor
the rand is the currency of South Africa

explanation.surface: A doctor and a relative steal some South African cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pinched' looks like theft but means held between G and P.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandpa is a grandfather, a family member.

clue.text: Framework turned regularly on inverted ledge

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter starting with the first
in a down clue inverted means turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: a sill is a ledge below a window

explanation.surface: A frame is turned over now and then on an upturned shelf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes TRE from turned; 'inverted' makes SILL into LLIS.
explanation.definitionFit: A trellis is a lattice framework for climbing plants.

clue.text: Greek figure taking lead from Greek god

indicators.note: taking the lead from a word removes its first letter

parts.note: Morpheus is the Greek god of dreams

explanation.surface: A Greek character follows the example of a Greek deity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking lead from' looks like following an example; it removes the M from MORPHEUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Orpheus is the legendary musician of Greek myth who went to the underworld for Eurydice.

clue.text: Harsh film we walked out of

indicators.note: walked out of means left, so those letters are removed

parts.note: a western is a cowboy film
taken as written

explanation.surface: A film so bad we walked out was severely judged.
explanation.definitionFit: Stern means strict and severe, so harsh.

clue.text: Paints fish touring isle to the West

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the fish surround the island

parts.note: eels are fish

indicators.note: in an across clue going to the west means read right to left

parts.note: the Isle of Man is in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: Artists paint fish that tour a western island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the West' reads the island leftwards in an across clue; 'touring' puts that inside the fish. 'Paints' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: Enamels as a verb means coats with enamel, a kind of glossy paint.

clue.text: When to expect arrival of child owed fruit

definitions.text: When to expect arrival of child

parts.note: a debt that is due is owed
a date is the fruit of the date palm

explanation.surface: An expectant mother is owed fruit as her birth approaches.
explanation.definitionFit: The due date is the day a baby's birth is predicted.

clue.text: Gratify one with nude dancing across empty landing

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: across means spread over, so these letters lie around the others
dancing moves the letters about into a new order
empty leaves only the outer letters of the word

explanation.surface: Someone dances naked across a deserted landing to please themself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' makes NUDE into NDUE, which goes 'across' LG, the 'empty landing'.
explanation.definitionFit: To indulge someone is to satisfy their wishes, so gratify.

clue.text: Charles on throne with good woman? It reflects well

indicators.note: Charles on the throne puts KING after LOO in an across clue

parts.note: throne is a jokey word for a toilet, the loo
Charles is the British king
a lass is a girl or young woman

explanation.surface: The king on his throne with a good woman beside him is something that reflects well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'throne' is British slang for the toilet (LOO), not the royal seat. 'reflects well' sounds like a credit but means a mirror.
explanation.definitionFit: A looking glass is a mirror, which reflects light.
